<!-- pr-reviewer: d2e4ccff74982e2ebb4ab5a7eb7959cb82d6f878 -->
**Delta review (since `13a12a25`, which was reviewed clean): Ready for the maintainer to merge** (at the next cut - this is a `feat`).

Scope: the merge of main `ec0ef646` (read with `git show --remerge-diff`) and `d2e4ccff`. Built on the head trial-merged with current `origin/main` (`37482923`, which adds PR #1220 since the refresh). That merge is clean, with no conflicts.

### What looks good
- **`operation/job.rs` + `tool_gate.rs`:** main's #852 code now lives in `tool_gate::job_tool`, in main's order: `tool_of`, then `neck_of`, then `tool_body::judged`, then the #369 lathe-body refusal. Every op that is not a wire still goes through it, so no #852 or #369 check is skipped. Only a `WireContour` takes the condition branch, with an empty neck and no body, because it mounts no tool. `git diff origin/main HEAD -- job.rs` shows nothing else of main's dropped.
- **`stamp.rs` -> `stamp_tool::write`:** I compared main's `current_stamp` tool block (from `h.write(tool_name…)` through the #852 `tool_cutter::digest` line) with `stamp_tool::write` line by line, after mapping `&mut h` to `h`. The two are identical: 51 statements in the same order, and the neck digest is still last, after `tool_body::digest`. A stored stamp of an op that mounts a tool does not move. No test pins a literal stamp value (and `DefaultHasher` would make one brittle anyway). Equal code is the proof here.
- **Post refusal (the safety check):** I traced every post door. `post_setup` / `post_script`, `post_mounts` / `post_mounts_script` (the MCP `post` tool and the script `post` verb both go through `api::v_post` to `post_mounts*`), `post_per_op` / `post_per_op_script` and `stream_records` all call `op_streams`. `op_streams` calls `posting_family::family_at_post` before any record is built (`posting.rs:833`). I also probed this with a throwaway local test (not pushed) on a generated Die cut. **All 8 doors refuse.** That includes the three that take a caller's script, each forced to the built-in Fanuc milling post. Each returned `Die1: a Wire Contour operation posts through a wire EDM post, which is not built yet - nothing is posted`, and no file was written. A wire contour cannot post through a milling post on any path.
- **`fidelity_law.rs`:** `Section::WireEdm` is not excess-aware, the same as plasma: refused on a reduced-fidelity model, not judged loosely. `coarse_laws.rs`'s `refused` list now names `WireContour` (`d2e4ccff`), and the suite passes.
- **`lathe_voice.rs`:** a named `WireContour` arm is refused on a lathe post, and the table goes 28 to 29 (`lathe_voice_tests.rs`).
- **Icon:** `assets/ui/svg/op-wire-contour.svg` and its PNG are an original drawing on Tabler's grid: two guide blocks, a wire, and plate lines. It is listed in `icons.rs` (`WireContour => "op-wire-contour"`) and `op_icons.rs`. The `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` "Original artwork" section already covers every `assets/ui/svg/*.svg` and its PNG, so it needs no entry. No other PNG changed against main, and no snapshot PNG changed.
- **Fixture `S9`:** dropping `"undersize": 0.1` does not weaken the test. `S9` is used only to prove that a condition with no `wire_diameter` is refused at creation (`wire_contour.rs:190-191`), and it still states a gap and no wire diameter. The undersize played no part in that.
- **Goldens:** against `origin/main` only the PR's own `wire_contour_die.cl` / `wire_contour_punch.cl` (and the `golden/CLAUDE.md` rows) differ. The merge took main's goldens unchanged, including the #862 `contour_disc_hole` / `contour_tangential_lead` moves. `golden_cl` passes 26/26.
- **Kerf:** still read through `Edm::condition(.., &[Gap, WireDiameter])` (`wire_op.rs:80`), and it meets #560's bounds: `edm_conditions` and `edm_machine` pass.
- No process files, `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts or dependencies changed against main.

### Local results (head + `origin/main` 37482923, Windows, debug)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app/-ui/-motion/-post --no-run` | built clean |
| app `wire_contour` | 8 passed (+1 local probe, removed) |
| app `edm_conditions` / `edm_machine` | 1 / 5 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 26 passed |
| app `posting` / `per_op_files` / `setup_mounts_post` | 17 / 9 / 6 passed |
| app `coarse_laws` / `model_fidelity` | 6 / 9 passed |
| app `lathe_post_refusals` / `plasma_post_refusals` | 11 / 7 passed |
| app `operations` (stamp staleness tests) | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| app `--lib` (incl. `lathe_voice_tests`) | 146 passed |
| motion `--lib` | 202 passed, 1 ignored |
| ui `--lib` from `crates/ui` (incl. `op_icon_table`, ribbon icons) | 607 passed, 5 ignored |
| clippy `-p app -p post -p ui -p motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` | **partial, stopped at the time box:** motion suites ok. In the app step, 52 suites ran (452 tests passed, 0 failed) before I stopped it. Because the PR adds two shared golden files, the plan selects nearly every app suite (~300), and that does not fit a review box on a shared machine. The suites the delta touches were all run by name above. |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. Nothing pins the stamp bytes. A future edit to `stamp_tool::write` could change every stored stamp without failing a test. A golden of a known tool's digest (built with a fixed hasher) would make this check mechanical. Worth a P7 follow-up if wanted.
2. MCP `post` was checked by tracing the code (`mcp/tools.rs` `post` calls `api::v_post`, which calls `posting::post_mounts*`, which calls `op_streams`), not by an end-to-end MCP call on a wire document.
3. The full quick gate (every app suite plus the ui suites) was not finished here. The batch run on main after this merges at the cut will cover it.

**Stacked PRs:** the head `d2e4ccff`, merged with current main, builds, passes clippy and passes every suite above. It is a sound base for the stacked PRs. They should take `git merge` of this head (or of main after this merges) and re-gate. The resolved conflict areas (`job.rs`, `stamp.rs`, `posting.rs`, `golden_cl.rs`, `panes.rs`) are where they are most likely to conflict.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
